Yes, and we always wear safety helmets.

PL_A2_MINI_STORY_001.title: The Lost Puppy in the Park

transcript.text: One sunny afternoon, Ben and his sister Emma were walking through Green Park. Near the big oak tree, they heard a soft whimpering sound. Behind a green bush, they discovered a tiny brown puppy with a red collar. The puppy was shivering and seemed lost. Emma checked the shiny silver tag on its collar and found a telephone number. Ben used his mother’s phone to dial the number immediately. Within ten minutes, a worried elderly lady named Mrs. Clark arrived. She was overjoyed to see her beloved puppy, Toby, safe and sound. To thank the children, she offered them delicious homemade cookies and praised their kindness.

PL_A2_FOOD_002.title: Cooking Pho Soup with Grandpa

transcript.text: Mr. David, my grandfather taught me how to cook traditional beef pho soup last Sunday!
That sounds fascinating, Tom! What ingredients did you need for the broth?
We simmered beef bones for over four hours with ginger, cinnamon, star anise, and roasted onions.
No wonder it smells so aromatic! Did you prepare the fresh rice noodles as well?
Yes, we warmed the noodles, added tender beef slices, and garnished with spring onions and fresh herbs.
Cooking traditional meals is a wonderful way to preserve our cultural heritage, Tom.

PL_A2_ENVIRONMENT_003.title: Our Green School Project

transcript.text: Good morning, Lily. How is our school recycling campaign progressing this week?
Good morning, Ms. Sarah. We have already collected over five hundred plastic bottles and forty kilograms of used paper.
That is remarkable! What are the students planning to do with all those recyclable materials?
The art club will transform the plastic bottles into self-watering flowerpots for our rooftop garden. And we will send the paper to the local recycling plant.
Small eco-friendly actions can truly make a huge difference in protecting our environment. Keep up the brilliant work!
Thank you, Ms. Sarah. We want our school to be as clean and green as possible.

PL_A2_TRAVEL_004.title: A Journey by High-Speed Train

transcript.text: Lily, have you ever travelled on an express high-speed train?
Yes, I traveled from Da Nang to Nha Trang with my family last summer holiday.
Was the journey comfortable? How fast did it travel?
It was super smooth and quiet! The scenery outside the large glass windows looked breathtaking, with lush mountains on one side and the blue ocean on the other.
I hope modern trains will connect all our major cities in the future. It is so much faster than buses.
I agree, and trains generate significantly less carbon pollution than airplanes.

PL_A2_HISTORIC_005.title: Visiting the Temple of Literature

transcript.text: Welcome to Hanoi, young man. Are you visiting the historic Temple of Literature today?
Yes, sir! Our history teacher assigned us a research task about Vietnam’s first national university.
You will find eighty-two stone turtle stelae erected here, honouring brilliant scholars from centuries ago.
It is so serene here despite being located in the middle of a bustling modern city.
Indeed. It stands as an enduring monument to the value of education, perseverance, and respect for knowledge.
I feel inspired to study harder after seeing how ancient scholars dedicated their lives to learning.

PL_A2_WEATHER_006.title: Four Seasons Around the World

transcript.text: Throughout the year, our planet experiences magnificent seasonal changes. In spring, nature awakens with vibrant blooming blossoms and fresh green shoots. Summer brings warmth and long daylight hours, ideal for outdoor adventures and beach trips. When autumn arrives, tree leaves turn into brilliant shades of gold, amber, and crimson before gently falling. Finally, winter covers high mountains in sparkling white snow. Each unique season offers distinct weather patterns, teaching us to appreciate the ever-changing harmony of the natural world.
